title: Make the field mapping answer the product query
description: Choose a field, mapping, and dynamic-field policy. The lab shows which queries work, which structures are built, and when reindexing becomes necessary.

fields.label: Product title
fields.detail: Users search words, then sort or facet on the complete title.

fields.label: Order status
fields.detail: Applications filter and aggregate a controlled machine value.

fields.label: Product price
fields.detail: Users filter by a numeric range, sort, and compute summary metrics.

fields.label: Published timestamp
fields.detail: The query needs date math, ranges, ordering, and time histograms.

mappings.label: text
mappings.detail: Analyze a human-language value for relevance queries.

mappings.label: keyword + normalizer
mappings.detail: Keep one normalized exact term with doc values.

mappings.label: text + keyword subfield
mappings.detail: Build separate relevance and exact-value access paths.

mappings.label: scaled_float
mappings.detail: Store a bounded decimal as a scaled integer for numeric operations.

mappings.label: date
mappings.detail: Parse timestamps into a numeric time representation.

dynamicPolicies.label: Open dynamic mapping
dynamicPolicies.detail: Unknown fields create mappings from observed values.
dynamicPolicies.risk: One malformed or unbounded payload can create accidental types and mapping growth.

dynamicPolicies.label: Strict explicit mapping
dynamicPolicies.detail: Unknown fields fail until the schema contract is changed deliberately.
dynamicPolicies.risk: Deployments need coordinated schema changes, but field behavior stays reviewable.

dynamicPolicies.label: Bounded dynamic template
dynamicPolicies.detail: Known name patterns receive an explicit controlled mapping.
dynamicPolicies.risk: A broad template can still classify fields incorrectly; test representative payloads.
